**Visual evidence summary:**
- **White fluffy/cottony colonies** on the wheat leaf surface — characteristic powdery mycelium
- **Dark specks** embedded in the white growth — consistent with cleistothecia (sexual fruiting bodies of Blumeria graminis)
- **Brownish/tan areas** beneath the white growth — older lesion tissue dying
- The growth is **on** the leaf surface (epiphytic), not embedded in the tissue
- Distributed as **discrete patches** along the leaf

This pattern is definitively characteristic of **Powdery Mildew**. The white superficial mycelium with embedded black cleistothecia is the hallmark diagnostic feature distinguishing it from other wheat diseases.
